== Biography ==
* '''Name:''' Recorded as '''Johne Glasgow''' in the parish register. Spelling variants include '''John''' and '''Johne'''.
* '''Location:''' Kirknewton and East Calder catalogue label, Midlothian, Scotland.
* '''Relationships:''' Father of a son named '''Johne Glasgow''' who was christened in 1649 at Kirknewton and East Calder.
** Child: Johne (christening 22 Apr 1649, Kirknewton and East Calder, Midlothian, Scotland).<ref name="FS">"Scotland, Births and Baptisms, 1564–1950," FamilySearch index, entry for '''Johne Glasgow''' (christened 22 Apr 1649, Kirknewton and East Calder, Midlothian), father '''Johne Glasgow'''; database accessed 16 Sep 2021; https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:1:VQ4K-X6G</ref>
== Research Notes ==
=== Easter Newtoun household ===

Prefer John [[Glasgow-3610]], the adult father in the 1649 Kirknewton baptism, as Annah [[Glasgow-1439]]’s father at 96% subjective confidence. Findmypast’s transcript of John’s 22 April 1649 baptism names father Johne Glasgow and residence Easter Newtoune. Its transcript of Annah’s 20 June 1652 baptism names father Johne Glasgow and residence Easter Newtoun. The matching uncommon full paternal name, specific residence, parish and three-year interval strongly support one household. This is a combined identity inference across two child records, not a literal statement that the children were siblings. A different Johne in the same settlement or a transcription error remains possible.

The 96% concerns the record-defined father of the 1652 child and his identification with the adult father of the 1649 child. It does not identify that adult with the John baptised at Mid Calder in 1616, prove his own father, or establish Annah’s later identity as the 1676 bride. The transcripts name no mother. Issobell Porteous’s existing maternal attachment remains separately unproved; no maternity is transferred to other children. The earlier [[Glasgow-1084|John Glasgow]] account may represent the same adult, but its 1616-child-to-adult identity remains possible at 42%, rather than established. These are overlapping profile-identity propositions, not mutually exclusive biological fathers; the percentages must not be added or treated as independent evidence. Retain that account as an alternative and resolve the possible duplicate before any live family change. No profiles are merged.

The Findmypast transcript pages were inspected on 18 October 2026; the parish originals were not inspected. The provider gives archive OPR 689/20, item 1, pages 5 and 13, while the supplied ScotlandsPeople index gives parish 690, references 10/14 and 10/32. Preserve that reference discrepancy for original comparison. Both Findmypast pages label the place Kirknewton and East Calder. The extra indexed version of Annah’s baptism, R_686208660, also names Johne and leaves the mother blank; it is another derivative of the same event, not independent corroboration. The September daily-limit responses are historical access failures; these targeted transcript retries now succeeded, without completing the wider Findmypast audit.

This is one proposed confident father-profile replacement, not a newly discovered biological father, a new birth event, a new connected branch or an upgrade of [[Glasgow-3610|John Glasgow]]’s own 28% father hypothesis. His earlier 1608-child comparison, [[Glasgow-3296|John Glasgow]] father, the conditional 1616-child/[[Glasgow-991|James Glasgow]] alternative and all other ancestry grades remain unchanged. [[Glasgow-3012|John Glasgow]]’s existing 98% father role remains unchanged. All birth and death fields, mothers and saved WikiTree family fields are preserved. [[Glasgow-3112|Margaret Glasgow]]’s competing 1646/1649 readings are unresolved: her 26 November 1649 Findmypast transcript names John and Kirknewton/East Calder, but gives no residence. It does not independently place her in the Easter Newtoun household.

Compare the original 1649 and 1652 entries, their register references and neighbouring households; look for a recorded mother, occupation or witness tying the Easter Newtoun adult to the 1642 Porteous marriage and 1616 baptism. Shared residence alone does not choose his grandparents.<ref name="EasterNewton2026">[https://www.findmypast.co.uk/transcript?id=SCOT%2FOPR%2FBAP%2F4473470 Findmypast, Scotland Parish Births & Baptisms, John, 22 April 1649, Kirknewton and East Calder, provider OPR 689/20 item 1 p.5; transcript inspected 18 October 2026, original uninspected]; [https://www.findmypast.co.uk/transcript?id=SCOT%2FOPR%2FBAP%2F4473604 Findmypast, Scotland Parish Births & Baptisms, Annah, 20 June 1652, Kirknewton and East Calder, provider OPR 689/20 item 1 p.13; transcript inspected 18 October 2026, original uninspected]; [https://www.findmypast.co.uk/transcript?id=SCOT%2FOPR%2FBAP%2F4473472 Findmypast, Scotland Parish Births & Baptisms, Margaret, 26 November 1649, Kirknewton and East Calder, provider OPR 689/20 item 1 p.5; transcript inspected 18 October 2026, original uninspected]; [https://www.findmypast.co.uk/transcript?id=R_686208660 Findmypast, Annah, 20 June 1652, R_686208660; additional index version, mother blank; inspected 18 October 2026].</ref>


=== Father relationship confidence review — 16 October 2026 ===

The existing father relationship from [[Glasgow-3012|Johne Glasgow, indexed in 1649]] to [[Glasgow-3610|Johne Glasgow, the 1649 father]] is now documented locally for the record-defined 1649 child. The supplied Scotland’s People index, Kirknewton and East Calder OPR 690/10/14, FR 15, names JOHNE GLASGOW as parent of the child JOHNE indexed on 22 April 1649. The preserved FamilySearch VQ4K-X6G account agrees on the child, father, parish and date. These are two presentations of the same underlying register, not independent records. [[Glasgow-3610|Johne Glasgow, the 1649 father]] is specifically the adult-father account defined by that entry. No inference from age or surname is needed for that parental role.

This certainty applies to the child and father in the 1649 record. It does not prove that the child became the 1673 Margaret Currie husband or that the father was the 1608 Mid Calder child, nor does it identify his own parents. The selected [[Glasgow-3610|Johne Glasgow, the 1649 father]]→[[Glasgow-3296|Glasgow-3296]] link remains uncertain. The profile’s 4 April 1649 birth and the index’s 22 April date remain unreconciled; neither the birth date nor the birth/baptism distinction is changed. The mother is not named in this index. The original register was not newly inspected; the confidence assessment rests on the maintained named-parent index evidence, with those limits explicit.

The six highest-impact selected father hypotheses were re-evaluated using their actual source wording and identity assumptions. None has sufficient evidence for an overall certainty upgrade from this review. One existing, previously ungraded named-parent relationship inside the largest branch is newly marked documented locally; no new connection or working family is added. The live WikiTree certainty flag is unchanged and remains a pending amendment. Working and confidently marked connectivity are measured separately. [https://glasgow.phenotype.dev/branches/early-scottish-records/#major-connection-confidence-review Confidence review and source limits]. <ref>Maintained named-parent register index accounts: [https://www.scotlandspeople.gov.uk/ Scotland’s People supplied OPR index: Johne, 22 April 1649, Kirknewton/East Calder 690/10/14, FR 15; parent JOHNE GLASGOW; maintained 10 September 2026 review]; [https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:1:VQ4K-X6G FamilySearch VQ4K-X6G: preserved 1649 Johne/John father-and-child index account; not a newly inspected original]. No original manuscript newly inspected; same-register dependence, unresolved dates and child/adult identity limits remain explicit.</ref>


=== Selected uncertain Lothian family —16 October2026 ===

Select John [[Glasgow-3610]] as the uncertain working father of William [[Glasgow-1026]], the older Kirknewton householder associated with Ann McCook by 1682. This activates the same-parish candidate already retained in William’s research. A 1649 Kirknewton/East Calder index names Johne Glasgow as the father of the child Johne; the adult account also carries a Margaret comparison with unresolved 1646/1649 dates. A father active in 1649 could have another son around William’s estimated 1660 birth. If the adult John is the 1608 Mid Calder child used in his own selected family model, he would have been about 52 in 1660, chronologically possible for a father. That childhood identity is itself uncertain and is not required for the local parent generation to remain possible. The common parish setting and compatible parent generation favour this existing John comparison over restoring the younger Walter-1554 as William’s father or importing the weak Kilwinning John-1604 comparison. Select John at low confidence. No inspected baptism, marriage, testament or property record names William as this John’s son. Both father selections are expressly uncertain local hypotheses using existing material. No new mother, original inspection, live WikiTree edit, identity merge or confidence upgrade is claimed. The fixed cohort and all confidently marked connectivity measurements must remain unchanged. Counts describe retained profile accounts and inherit uncertainty in older links, including possible duplicates. [https://glasgow.phenotype.dev/branches/early-scottish-records/#lothian-family-heads Full comparison and surviving alternatives]. <ref>Existing reviewed indexes: [https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:1:VQ4V-PQK Johnne,Inveresk 1632], SP 689,10/226; [https://familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:1:XTPF-7YB Jean,Edinburgh 1677], James/Isobell Duffe household; [https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:1:VQ4K-X6G Johne,Kirknewton 1649], father Johne; [https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:1:VQ4K-ZQN Bessie,Kirknewton 1682], William/Ann household. These support explicitly uncertain generation/locality selections, not direct parent clauses for the two adults; no original newly inspected.</ref>


* '''Birth and parentage:''' His exact birth date and birthplace are unknown. The 'before 1629' date is an uncertain adulthood estimate inherited from the 1646-child comparison; Margaret's competing 1646/1649 readings leave that basis unresolved. It is not a baptism or proved birth date. The former exact 18 February 1626 date and attachment as a son of [[Glasgow-1087|William Glasgow]], christened in 1609, had no cited record and were removed on 26 September 2026. The baptism names the adult only as the child's father.
* '''Mother of the child:''' The 1649 entry names only the father. The mother’s name does not appear in this index. Check the original Old Parish Register image on ScotlandsPeople in case the manuscript includes the mother.
* '''Parish coverage:''' Kirknewton and East Calder OPRs can have gaps and spelling variation. Search for:
** Marriages for a '''John/Johne Glasgow''' in Kirknewton and East Calder in the two decades before 1649.
** Additional baptisms to a father named '''Johne/John Glasgow''' in the same parish, 1635–1665, to identify siblings.
** Testaments and sasines in Midlothian that mention a John/Johne Glasgow of Kirknewton or East Calder.
* '''Name variants to include in searches:''' Glasgow, Glasco, Glascow, Glescow; forename John, Johne, Jon, Jo.
=== Selected uncertain working father,15 October2026 ===
[[Glasgow-3296|John Glasgow, Mid Calder/Quothquan working identity]] is selected as the working father in the local research model. The older John represents the father named in the Mid Calder baptisms of 1608–1609 as an uncertain earlier identity. The 1608 child, provisionally carried by John-1086, is a viable earlier identity for the adult John named as father in neighbouring Kirknewton/East Calder in 1649: age 40–41 is straightforward. Retain the older John as uncertain working father on that local and chronological reconstruction. The 17 October review retains 28% and corrects the earlier reliance on a supposed 1646–1650 child sequence. Keep the two son profiles separate while testing their possible identity.

This is a hypothesis from existing material, not a parent named in a newly found record. John-1086 primarily represents the 1685 Quothquan decedent, whose identity with the 1608 child and with3610 remains unproved. They may be different men, and the older father’s Mid Calder/Montfoid/Quothquan identity is itself uncertain. Robert-4006 is another generationally compatible Calder father. This does not restore the former unsupported William-1087 father or treat1629 as a recorded birthday. No mother or live WikiTree parent-field change is implied. The earlier proof-based rationale remains superseded where corrected.

=== Identity and parentage comparison — 17 October 2026 ===

[[Glasgow-3296|John Glasgow, the Mid Calder/Quothquan working identity]] remains the selected uncertain father, assessed at '''28% subjective probability'''. The child Jhone baptised on 26 June 1608 at Mid Calder would have been about 40–41 when this adult Johne was named as a father at neighbouring Kirknewton/East Calder in 1649. This fits a local family reconstruction, but the identification of that child with the 1649 father and of the Mid Calder father with the 1650 Quothquan man are separate unresolved steps. No shared occupation, holding, spouse, witness or documented sibling joins these accounts.<ref name="MidCalder1608">“Scotland, Births and Baptisms, 1564–1950,” FamilySearch, [https://familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:1:X1BL-X8B Jhone Glasgow, 1608, father Jhone]; supplied Scotland's People index, Mid Calder OPR 694/10/12, 26 June 1608; Findmypast, [https://www.findmypast.co.uk/transcript?id=SCOT%2FOPR%2FBAP%2F4585634&tab=this SCOT/OPR/BAP/4585634], OPR 694/1, item 3, p.5. Derivative presentations of the same register.</ref><ref name="FS" /> The 28% assessment retains the earlier uncertain selection without a confidence upgrade.

The index-proved 1649 father–child role does not identify either person's earlier or later life. The 1650 Quothquan testament names John's sister Bessie but no child or parent; the 1685 Quothquan testament of [[Glasgow-1086|John Glasgow]] names his widow Jonet, surname provisionally read Kinnie, but no child or parent. They are distinct record-defined adults, each with a proposed Mid Calder connection. The omission of children in 1650 does not disprove this family.<ref>National Records of Scotland, Lanark Commissary Court, CC14/5/5, images65–66, John Glasgow in Quodquen, confirmed 27 May 1650; CC14/5/12, images67–68, John Glasgow in Quothquan, proceeding dated 25 March 1685. Existing transcriptions; [https://www.scotlandspeople.gov.uk/search-records/legal-records/wills Scotland's People wills search]. No original newly inspected for this comparison.</ref>

[[Glasgow-1084|John Glasgow]], the Mid Calder child recorded on 18 February 1616, is a compatible alternative identity. His entry names [[Glasgow-991|James Glasgow]] as father. His proposed adult account includes John Glasgow and [[Porteous-912|Issobell Porteous]] in the Edinburgh marriage index of 30 June 1642, followed by their daughter [[Glasgow-1438|Issobell]] on 4 April 1643. A father aged about 33 in 1649 fits this alternative.<ref>National Records of Scotland, supplied Scotland's People Old Parish Register indexes: Mid Calder, John Glasgow, 18 February 1616, father James, OPR 694/10/28; Edinburgh, Johnne Glasgow and Issobell Porteous, 30 June 1642, OPR 685/1/430/244, FR848; [https://www.scotlandspeople.gov.uk/ repository]. Original pages not inspected for this review.</ref><ref>“Scotland, Births and Baptisms, 1564–1950,” FamilySearch, [https://familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:1:X1YN-JHD Issobell Glasgow, 4 April 1643, Edinburgh], parents John Glasgow and Issobell Porteous.</ref> The attributed daughter [[Glasgow-1439|Anne]], 20 June 1652 under the Kirknewton/East Calder label, currently rests on a FamilySearch tree citation, not an inspected parish entry.<ref>FamilySearch tree, [https://www.familysearch.org/tree/person/details/4XPK-FW2 Anne Glasgow, attributed 20 June 1652 occurrence]; a tree lead, not original-register evidence.</ref> This leaves James as an unselected father alternative conditional on the adult identification, without assigning a separate percentage, merging the Johns, replacing the selected father or identifying a mother. The proposed continuity of the separate 1638 John/[[Patoune-11|Helene Patoune]] household with the Porteous household also remains uncertain.

[[Glasgow-4006|Robert Glasgow]] remains a compatible father-generation comparison without a named son John. [[Glasgow-3056|John Glasgow]], the 1617 Linlithgow child of [[Glasgow-1561|John Glasgow]], is another compatible childhood comparison; his attributed 1670 death is itself uncertain.<ref>“Scotland, Births and Baptisms, 1564–1950,” FamilySearch, [https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:1:X1RV-T85 John Glesgow, 1617, Linlithgow]; supplied Scotland's People death/burial index, Linlithgow OPR 668/70/653, 14 February 1670, unnamed Glasgow with John Glasgow in the parents/other field, age blank. Original uninspected; death attribution uncertain.</ref> [[Glasgow-1087|William Glasgow]], baptised in 1609, remains an unsupported former father; his baptism date alone does not biologically exclude fathering a son before 1629.

There is no proved 1646–1650 baptism sequence for this household. [[Glasgow-3112|Margaret Glasgow]] has competing 11 November 1646 and 26 November 1649 readings. [[Glasgow-3118|Alexander Glasgow]] has an estimated circa-1650 birth from his 1667 marriage, not a proved 1650 baptism. Neither supplies an independent proved sibling bridge. The secure paternal occurrence used here is the 22 April 1649 index.<ref>Findmypast/Scottish Genealogy Society, [https://www.findmypast.co.uk/transcript?id=SCOT%2FOPR%2FBAP%2F4473472 Margaret Glasgow, 26 November 1649], father John Glasgow, Kirknewton and East Calder, OPR 689/20, p.5; this conflicts with the maintained FamilySearch-based 11 November 1646 account. FamilySearch, [https://familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:1:XY9W-TPB Alexander Glasgow and Margaret Smith, 1667 marriage index]; supplied Scotland's People OPR 690/10/54, 18 October 1667, FR37.</ref> Original register context and the Porteous household may supply distinguishing residences, occupations, witnesses or family associations.

=== Dates, locality and source context ===

* '''Location:''' Kirknewton and East Calder Parish, Midlothian, Scotland.
* '''Birth and parentage:''' His exact birth date and birthplace are unknown. The structured 'before 1629' date is an uncertain adulthood estimate based on children baptised from 1646; it is not a baptism or proved birth date. The former exact 18 February 1626 date and attachment as a son of [[Glasgow-1087|William Glasgow]], christened in 1609, had no cited record and were removed on 26 September 2026. The baptism names the adult only as the child's father.
